claim.markdown_says: ## 8.1.3 COBOL character repertoire  -- emitted at markdown level 2, i.e. SHALLOWER than its own parent '### 8.1 Character sets' (line 4973) and at the same level as the clause heading '## 8 Language fundamentals' (line 4967).
claim.why_it_matters: The heading depth is inverted relative to the standard's own numbering, so any tool that builds a table of contents, a section index, or a spec-citation resolver from the markdown headings will place 8.1.3 as a peer of Clause 8 rather than as a child of 8.1. The same inversion repeats on the neighbouring pages of this batch: '## 8.1.3.2 General rules' (p.121, line 5131) sits at level 2 while its sibling '### 8.1.3.1 General' (p.120, line 5082) sits at level 3; '## 8.1.4 Alphabets' and '## 8.1.5 Collating sequences' (p.123, lines 5178/5183) sit at level 2 while their siblings 8.1.1/8.1.2 sit at level 3; and '## 8.2.2 Locale field names' (p.125, line 5256) sits at level 2 while its sibling '### 8.2.1 General' (p.124, line 5210) sits at level 3. The heading TEXT and numbering are all correct - only the markdown level is wrong - so this is navigational, not normative. It appears to be a document-wide transcription pattern rather than a defect unique to these pages; fixing it should be done as one mechanical sweep, not page by page.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. Nothing is missing and no content differs; the difference is markdown presentation markup only, which the rejection criteria exclude. (1) THE HEADING IS PRESENT AND VERBATIM CORRECT. Rendered specs/ISO_COBOL.pdf page 120 (printed page 90) at 300dpi. Every heading printed on the page is present in the markdown: '8.1.3 COBOL character repertoire' -> line 5079, '8.1.3.1 General' -> line 5082, 'Table 1 - COBOL character repertoire' -> line 5088. The heading text, the clause number, the page assignment and the ordering all match the PDF exactly. The claim is filed as kind='missing-heading' but no heading, and no character of any heading, is missing. The kind label is a misclassification of its own evidence. (2) THE PDF DOES NOT ENCODE THE DEPTH THE CLAIM SAYS IT ENCODES. I cropped and zoomed the two headings (E:/Temp/specrecon/v120/headings_zoom.png) and looked at the printed glyphs. '8.1.3 COBOL character repertoire' and '8.1.3.1 General' are set in the SAME bold serif face, at the SAME point size, at the SAME flush-left margin, with the SAME tab gap after the number. There is no typographic level cue distinguishing a third-level from a fourth-level subclause anywhere on this page. The 'level-3 subclause' in the claim's pdf_says is an inference the reviewer drew from the dotted number - it is not something the PDF prints. The dotted number is the only depth carrier in the source, and the markdown reproduces it exactly. So on the one channel where the PDF actually carries depth, the two documents agree perfectly. (3) THE MARKDOWN CARRIES THE HIERARCHY LOSSLESSLY, IN THE ANCHORS. Line 5078 is . I checked this across the whole file: all 2098 numbered headings in specs/ISO_COBOL.md have a section anchor immediately above them - 2098 of 2098, zero exceptions. The anchor slug encodes the full path (section-8-1-3 is unambiguously a child of section-8-1, itself a child of section-8). Any citation resolver or index builder has an exact, complete, machine-readable hierarchy available; the '#' count is redundant decoration next to it. (4) THE CLAIMED DOWNSTREAM HARM IS NOT AVAILABLE TO BE HARMED. The claim's stated stake is that a TOC/index/citation resolver built from markdown heading nesting would misplace 8.1.3. No such tool could ever have been built on this file: the transcription emits the running header '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' as an H1 941 times and the page marker '## Page N' as an H2 1233 times. Heading nesting in this document is already saturated with per-page furniture at H1/H2 on essentially every page, so it is provably not the structure carrier and was never usable as one. Re-leveling 8.1.3 to H3 would not make heading-derived navigation work; it would still be swamped by 941 H1 page banners. (5) THE CLAIM MISQUOTES ITS OWN SOURCE AND MISDESCRIBES THE PATTERN. Line 4967 is not '## 8 Language fundamentals' - it is the running header '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)'. The clause heading is at line 4970. More substantively: I measured the numbering-depth-to-heading-level mapping across the entire file and it is not an 'inversion', it is unstructured noise. Depth-3 numbers are emitted as H2 276 times, H3 508 times and H4 17 times; depth-4 as H2 162 / H3 620 / H4 24; depth-5 as H2 118 / H3 128 / H4 41; depth-2 as H2 162 / H3 26. The claim also missed that '## 8.2 Locales' is itself H2 while its direct sibling-in-depth '### 8.1 Character sets' is H3 - i.e. the two second-level clause headings on either side of this very passage disagree with each other. There is no rule being violated here because there is no rule being followed anywhere; the '#' count is an artifact of the extraction pipeline's per-page heuristics and is uncorrelated with clause depth throughout all ~2100 headings. CONCLUSION: page 120 of the markdown is a faithful transcription of page 120 of the PDF. No text is missing, no text is altered, no numbering is wrong, and no normative meaning is affected - the claim concedes the last point itself ('navigational, not normative'). This is formatting, and formatting-only differences are an explicit rejection criterion. If the owner later wants uniform '#' depth derived from the dotted number, that is a cosmetic normalization of the extraction pipeline applied to ~2098 headings at once - it is not a spec-reconciliation discrepancy and should not consume a ledger slot or be recorded as a defect against this page or this batch.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. PDF page 120 prints '8.1.3 COBOL character repertoire' and '8.1.3.1 General' in identical bold serif at identical size and identical flush-left margin - the PDF carries subclause depth ONLY in the dotted number, which specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 5079 reproduces verbatim, preceded by an exact anchor. Nothing is missing; the heading text, number, order and page are all correct. The only difference is the number of '#' characters, i.e. markdown presentation markup, which is uncorrelated with clause depth throughout the entire transcription (depth-3 clause numbers are emitted as H2 276x / H3 508x / H4 17x across the file; all 2098 numbered headings nonetheless carry a correct section anchor). The claim's premise that a heading-derived TOC or citation resolver is at risk does not hold, because the file already emits 941 H1 running headers and 1233 H2 page markers, so heading nesting is not and never was the structure carrier. The claim also misquotes line 4967 as '## 8 Language fundamentals' (that line is the running header; the clause heading is line 4970).
